questions: Should the function handle non-string elements in the numpy array (e.g., numeric types, None) by converting them to strings, raising an error, or something else?

If a string contains consecutive '.' separators (e.g., 'a..b'), should the resulting reversed string preserve the multiple '.' as separators (producing empty segments) or treat them as a single separator?
Should the function modify the input array in-place or return a new array?
Is the function expected to handle numpy arrays of any shape (e.g., 2D, 3D) or only 1D arrays?
Should leading or trailing '.' in strings be preserved in the reversed output (e.g., '.a.b.' becomes '.b.a.' or 'b.a')?
Are there any constraints on performance or memory usage for large arrays?
Should the function treat '.' as a separator only, or could it be escaped (e.g., '\.') to represent a literal dot within a word?
If the input array is empty (size 0), should the function return an empty array of the same shape/dtype or raise an error?
